go-verifier-provenance.hypothesis: Reusable-workflow confused deputy: SourceRepositoryURI is never compared with the trusted repo, so a workflow_call workflow in a tinfoilsh repo invoked from an attacker repo would carry the trusted SAN
go-verifier-provenance.why_rejected: No public tinfoilsh repository has any `on: workflow_call` workflow (grep over all 100 clones); measure-image-action and update-container-action are composite actions whose SAN is the caller's workflow. Hardening note only.

go-verifier-provenance.hypothesis: Any workflow file under .github/workflows/ on any tag is accepted (signingIdentity uses [^/@]+), so `test.yml` with `on: push` running on a tag push, or fork PRs, could mint the trusted identity
go-verifier-provenance.why_rejected: id-token is never granted by default; test workflows do not request it; fork pull_request runs get no OIDC token and pull_request_target/issue triggers run on refs/heads/*, which the refs/tags/ pattern and authenticatedArtifact reject. Tag push, release and workflow_dispatch all require write access (the trusted release authority).

go-verifier-provenance.hypothesis: tinfoil-config commit 043b28e (remove runtime cvm-source overrides) implies a host-exploitable image-source override
go-verifier-provenance.why_rejected: cvm-source lived inside the measured config (included verbatim in the signed deployment and hashed into the cmdline); measure-image-action fetched the manifest with `gh attestation verify -R <repo>` and the launch measurement covers kernel/initrd regardless of where tinfoild sources them. No verifier trusts cvm-source; tinfoild is private so no host-side path could be shown.

go-verifier-provenance.hypothesis: Freshness witness replay by editing tlog integratedTime (Rekor v2 has no SET)
go-verifier-provenance.why_rejected: sigstore-go v1.2.2 tlog.go:213 only emits a Tlog timestamp for SET-verified Rekor v1 entries; validateFreshnessTime takes the earliest such timestamp and requires at least one, so Rekor v2-only bundles fail closed and v1 times are signed.

go-verifier-provenance.hypothesis: Parser differential between sigstore-go's protojson statement and tinfoil-go's json/v2 freshness parser (duplicate keys, multiple subjects)
go-verifier-provenance.why_rejected: Both reject duplicate members; enforceSubject0Digest re-checks subject[0]; freshness requires exactly one subject with matching name and digest; witness predicate must match repo/tag/commit/subject of the authenticated code artifact.

go-verifier-provenance.hypothesis: Platform-endorsements v2 (IGVM, no host_data/platform_measurements) or the new config-endorsement collateral offers a weaker registry-approval path in Go
go-verifier-provenance.why_rejected: AuthenticatePlatformEndorsements rejects any predicate other than platform-endorsements/v1; ConfigEndorsementV1Format is not decoded; tinfoil-config/endorsement has no consumer in any public repo.

go-verifier-provenance.hypothesis: freshness.yml trusts repo/tag/digest inputs without checking the digest belongs to that release
go-verifier-provenance.why_rejected: By design: the control plane (Actions-write token) selects what to witness; the verifier still requires a genuine tinfoilsh-signed artifact for the same repo/tag/commit/digest, so the control plane can only choose among real releases (which is exactly what makes the catalog finding work).

go-verifier-provenance.hypothesis: Tag/digest hints in the document (SigstoreRef.Repo/Tag/Digest) could steer verification to another repo
go-verifier-provenance.why_rejected: Repo for code comes from the caller; platform repo must equal tinfoilsh/platform-endorsements; tag hint must equal the cert's SourceRepositoryRef; digest must equal subject[0].

go-verifier-provenance.hypothesis: SEV/TDX expectation assembly accepts malformed or empty signed registers
go-verifier-provenance.why_rejected: policy.DecodeHex enforces exactly 48 bytes for every register; machine identity must be in the endorsed machines map; MRTD/RTMR0 must match an endorsed platform measurement for the declared shape.

go-verifier-provenance.hypothesis: SCT duplicate-log guard or legacy bundle checks can be bypassed
go-verifier-provenance.why_rejected: Bundles with x509CertificateChain are rejected; exactly one DSSE signature required; duplicate SCT log IDs rejected; sigstore-go also requires 1 SCT, 1 tlog entry and 1 observer timestamp.

webapp-render-xss.hypothesis: rehype-katex runs after rehype-sanitize, so KaTeX output could smuggle href/src/style/event attributes (trust:false, strict:false, output htmlAndMathml)
webapp-render-xss.why_rejected: katex 0.16.47 fuzzed with 17 trust-sensitive payloads (\href, \url, \includegraphics, \htmlStyle/\htmlData/\htmlId/\htmlClass, \color/\textcolor with url(), macro expansion, attribute-breakout strings): 0/17 produced URL/event-bearing markup; colours are restricted to hex/word, sizes are numeric (work/webapp-render-xss/katex-fuzz/output.txt).

webapp-render-xss.hypothesis: Script execution in the app origin via HTML injection through rehype-raw
webapp-render-xss.why_rejected: rehype-sanitize defaultSchema strips script/style/iframe/object/event/style attributes (confirmed by the repo's own preview-rendering test and my DOM dump); production CSP is script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval' with no unsafe-inline and no user-controlled same-origin scripts, so even an injection could not execute script (browser PoC shows inline script blocked).

webapp-render-xss.hypothesis: javascript:/data: links via <a href> or the preprocessMarkdown <a href>→markdown rewrite
webapp-render-xss.why_rejected: react-markdown defaultUrlTransform drops non-http(s)/mailto/tel/irc/xmpp schemes and the custom `a` component additionally applies @braintree/sanitize-url 7.1.2 (javascript: → about:blank).

webapp-render-xss.hypothesis: Mermaid preview XSS (mermaid 11.16.1) in the app origin
webapp-render-xss.why_rejected: Renders inside /preview/mermaid.html framed with sandbox=allow-scripts and served (vercel.json) with `default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; sandbox allow-scripts; frame-ancestors 'self'`, securityLevel strict, htmlLabels false: opaque origin, no network, no popups/top-navigation.

webapp-render-xss.hypothesis: SVG code-fence preview (auto-opened) loads external resources or scripts
webapp-render-xss.why_rejected: DOMPurify svg profile then rendered as — SVG-as-image cannot fetch external resources or run script.

webapp-render-xss.hypothesis: HTML/JS code previews and HTML artifacts exfiltrate or escape
webapp-render-xss.why_rejected: They run on webapp-sandbox.tinfoil.sh in opaque-origin frames and start in code/source view (click required); nested html/js documents carry `default-src 'none'` meta CSPs; artifact documents can load https images but only after an explicit Preview click.

webapp-render-xss.hypothesis: render_artifact_preview {type:'url'} auto-opens the sidebar and frames an attacker URL (or the sandbox /preview with an attacker nonce)
webapp-render-xss.why_rejected: Production frame-src allows only 'self', verification-center and the sandbox origins; framing the sandbox /preview via the url artifact gives the frame a different nonce than the hook's, so no run is ever posted; a framed verification-center page has origin 'null' in the sandboxed frame and verification-sidebar checks event.origin.

webapp-render-xss.hypothesis: MapView sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin" runs model HTML in a real origin
webapp-render-xss.why_rejected: src is the sandbox origin's /map page (MapKit), model data arrives only as JSON locations via postMessage, and a consent dialog gates the load.

webapp-render-xss.hypothesis: Citation pills / favicons leak the full URL to the attacker
webapp-render-xss.why_rejected: Favicon requests go to the opengraph-metadata enclave which fetches icons.duckduckgo.com/ip3/<host>.ico (confidential-website-metadata-fetcher handlers.go:185) — only the hostname leaks, via DuckDuckGo, without the user's IP (weak subdomain channel; noted inside candidate 1 only).

webapp-render-xss.hypothesis: RecipeCard print path uses document.write(html) into a window.open popup (same-origin about:blank XSS)
webapp-render-xss.why_rejected: window.open('', '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer') returns null in current browsers so the code path is unreachable; a reachable about:blank would also inherit the opener's CSP.

webapp-render-xss.hypothesis: postMessage listeners accept spoofed frames (preview outputs, verification document)
webapp-render-xss.why_rejected: use-preview-messages/sandbox-frame check event.source === iframe.contentWindow plus instanceId/nonce and bound output to ≤1000 text lines; verification-sidebar checks event.origin === verification-center origin.

webapp-render-xss.hypothesis: html2pdf export (html2pdf.js 0.14.0 / html2canvas 1.4.1) introduces a new sink
webapp-render-xss.why_rejected: Operates on a clone of the already-rendered DOM with CSSOM-only style changes; adds no attacker-controlled HTML and no channel beyond the existing image loads.

webapp-render-xss.hypothesis: Shared chats let another user attack the viewer
webapp-render-xss.why_rejected: Same renderer; an attacker-sharer can only learn the viewer's IP/time via the image channel (content is already theirs) — low value, folded into candidate 1's model.

router.hypothesis: Unverified JWT `sub` in cacheSaltIdentity/jwtSubject (main.go) lets an attacker pick another tenant's prefix-cache namespace or skip rate limiting with a forged at+jwt
router.why_rejected: The enclave shim (cvmimage/tinfoil/cmd/shim/api.go + internal/key/jwt) verifies EdDSA signature via the control plane JWKS, issuer, aud https://inference.tinfoil.sh, scope inference:api and typ at+jwt before serving; a forged sub breaks the signature, so no inference (and no cache fill) happens.

router.hypothesis: Client-supplied cache_salt/user_cache_secret or unframed hashing lets a caller land in another tenant's vLLM prefix-cache namespace via the router
router.why_rejected: applyCacheSalt strips client cache_salt, pops user_cache_secret, and derives Sum(tag, tenant, secret) with length-prefixed framing (cachesalt.go); tenant = opaque key or verified JWT sub; gateway-mode (tinfoil-go sealTransport) uses a different domain tag over a 256-bit random secret, so namespaces cannot collide or be guessed.

router.hypothesis: Control-plane-served runtime config (UPDATE_CONFIG_URL) can add a model or an unattested host so plaintext leaves to a non-genuine enclave
router.why_rejected: sync() only iterates models from the embedded config.yml; every host must present an attestation whose measurement equals the sigstore-verified latest release of the pinned repo (manager.go addEnclave); the proxy/MCP/file-conversion/tokenize transports are all pinned to that attested TLS key. Config can only tune overload/cache_route/reservations.

router.hypothesis: Tool loop / MCP path exposes other tenants' data or lets a client forge X-Tinfoil-Tool-*/usage-context headers
router.why_rejected: Session registry, streamers and tool-call logs are per request (no package-level per-request state); MCP endpoints pinned unless --debug; usage-context headers are HMAC-signed with USAGE_CONTEXT_SECRET; client Authorization is overridden by the delegated token where applicable.

router.hypothesis: Code-execution profile leaks containerAuthToken/encryptionKey or reaches a sandbox
router.why_rejected: Model key 'code-execution' is absent from the embedded config.yml, so in the shipped router the profile fails closed (model not found) before any dial; dev log that would write these secrets is compiled out (toolruntime_debug tag not used by Dockerfile).

router.hypothesis: 'Safe document errors' path leaks another tenant's content or logs document text
router.why_rejected: upstreamDocumentError echoes <=512 bytes of the doc-upload enclave's 4xx body for the caller's own document, replaces 5xx with a generic message, and writeError logs only status/type/code/param.

router.hypothesis: Safeguards capture exfiltrates first-party chat transcripts to the unattested control plane
router.why_rejected: Router submits transcript + credential only to the in-enclave sidecar (http://safeguards:8090); confidential-safeguards reports only {credential, conversation_id} to api.tinfoil.sh on a confirmed violation.

router.hypothesis: Usage reporting / unknown-model reports leak secrets to an unattested party
router.why_rejected: They carry raw customer API keys, but only to api.tinfoil.sh (the issuer) over HMAC-signed requests with redirects disabled; by design, no third party.

router.hypothesis: Rate-limit bypass via the route-context cache (cold entries admit, async refresh, JWT skip)
router.why_rejected: Only a short cold-window burst against the shared RPM/TPM layer; the enclave shim still validates opaque keys online per request; first-party at+jwt tokens are deliberately unmetered on the inference path (router skips lookup, shim validates locally) which is a product-policy question needing the closed control plane, not a confidentiality bug.

router.hypothesis: Streaming response mixing across requests (SSE heartbeat, usage trailer, token extractor)
router.why_rejected: All writers/extractors are per request; heartbeatWriter serialises writes with a mutex; no shared buffers found.

router.hypothesis: confidential-openai-adapter: shim nil authenticated-endpoints leaves /v1/responses etc. unauthenticated, enabling an open relay or cache-namespace sharing
router.why_rejected: The adapter forwards only requests with a non-empty Authorization and the model enclave validates the key; cache scope is HMAC(per-process root, Authorization header) so distinct keys get distinct namespaces. Plaintext-replay exposure is already Finding 1.

router.hypothesis: inference-sidecar / usage-reporting-go contain an exploitable flaw
router.why_rejected: Sidecar is loopback-only inside the model CVM with no auth role (pads SSE, filters usage chunk); usage-reporting-go signs batches over method/path/reporter/timestamp/nonce/body hash with constant-time verification; nothing reachable by an external attacker.

Hosts come only from attested config entries; model names must exist in the embedded catalog; file inputs accept only base64/data: URLs (no fetch); X-Tinfoil-Model is only an equality check; Director sets req.Host to the configured host.

webapp-network-trust.hypothesis: Verification fails open via cached document (getCachedVerificationDocument / terminalCachedDoc?.securityVerified retry) or error paths still send messages
webapp-network-trust.why_rejected: The sidebar logic only drives the UI badge; every production send goes through SecureClient.fetch (tinfoil-client.ts initClient -> new OpenAI({fetch: secureClient.fetch}) or the recoverable transport), and SecureClient.fetch awaits ready(), which rejects when verifyBundle throws, so no transport exists without a successful attestation; the dev simulator/local-router bypass is gated on NEXT_PUBLIC_DEV plus a localhost/private runtime origin and hosted builds reject the flag (next.config.mjs:17-21, config.ts:4-16).

webapp-network-trust.hypothesis: Verified HPKE key not bound to the connection / DNS-TLS attacker can serve a fake enclave because the ATC-chosen domain is unauthenticated (enclaveCert chain is not validated in cert-verify.ts)
webapp-network-trust.why_rejected: In EHBP mode the request body is sealed to the HPKE key taken from the AMD-signed REPORT_DATA and responses are AEAD-bound to the HPKE context (ehbp identity.js), so a WebPKI/DNS-level peer or a malicious ATC only sees headers (session token, X-Session-Id, X-Conversation-Id) and ciphertext and can replay/truncate; CSP connect-src limits the chosen domain to *.tinfoil.sh. Sigstore/SEV verification internals were out of scope here.

webapp-network-trust.hypothesis: EHBP JS response forgery analogous to Go Finding 4 (nonce-less non-2xx pass-through, 3xx handling)
webapp-network-trust.why_rejected: ehbp 0.3.3 client.js:92-101 passes through only non-2xx responses without a nonce and throws ProtocolError for 2xx without a nonce; browsers follow 3xx transparently so the chain ends in a nonce-less 2xx (fail closed) or an error status; openai-node throws APIError for >=400 and the webapp only displays error.message as text (stream-error-banner.tsx:279), no data acted on.

webapp-network-trust.hypothesis: Bodyless requests (GET/DELETE) through EHBP get plaintext, unauthenticated responses from the sync/model enclaves
webapp-network-trust.why_rejected: All sync RPCs are POST with JSON bodies (sync-api.ts; only /v1/health uses GET), chat/speech/doc-upload are POSTs; nothing security-relevant travels in a bodyless response.

webapp-network-trust.hypothesis: Browser-side analogue of the Go GetBody plaintext replay on HTTP/2 REFUSED_STREAM/GOAWAY
webapp-network-trust.why_rejected: The ehbp JS Transport serializes the ciphertext into the Request before fetch(); any browser-level retry re-sends the same ciphertext bytes, the plaintext never exists at the fetch layer.

webapp-network-trust.hypothesis: Plaintext chat data reaches a non-attested endpoint (title generation, thoughts summary, link previews, search, attachments, sharing, feedback, analytics)
webapp-network-trust.why_rejected: Titles/thought summaries go to summarizer.tinfoil.sh via SecureClient with configRepo pinned (summary-client.ts), memory facts via the attested router, link metadata/favicons via the opengraph-metadata enclave, search/attachments/share-seal/share-open via the attested sync enclave with sealed bodies; the control plane only receives enclave-produced ciphertext (/api/shares, legacy encrypted attachments) and ids; bug reports are a mailto: link; Plausible excludes /, /newchat, /chat/*, /share/*, /project/*/chat/* (analytics-routes.ts) so only bare /project/<id> paths are reported (metadata).

webapp-network-trust.hypothesis: Clerk JWT leaks via headers/URLs or open redirect on sign-in
webapp-network-trust.why_rejected: authTokenManager only injects Authorization for api.tinfoil.sh and the attested sync enclave; sign-in redirect targets are restricted to same-origin relative paths without backslashes and message markers are stripped first (redirect-url.ts).

webapp-network-trust.hypothesis: Chat recovery through api.tinfoil.sh (control plane as EHBP relay) exposes responses
webapp-network-trust.why_rejected: The control plane stores only the HPKE-sealed response keyed by a 128-bit random X-Session-Id; the recovery token is wrapped under a CEK-derived AES-GCM key before syncing (chat-recovery-crypto.ts); the control plane learns timing/size/chat-id metadata only.

webapp-network-trust.hypothesis: Share feature server side / link format leaks the chat
webapp-network-trust.why_rejected: /share/<chatId>#v2:<64-hex key>: ciphertext is produced inside the sync enclave with a random key, stored on the control plane, and opened by sending key+ciphertext to the attested enclave; the key stays in the fragment and share pages are excluded from analytics.

webapp-network-trust.hypothesis: Local chat import worker: zip path traversal / prototype pollution
webapp-network-trust.why_rejected: Imports are JSON.parse'd and schema-validated in the browser (no filesystem, no recursive merge of untrusted keys found in local-tinfoil-import-parser.ts); shallow check only, nothing exploitable identified.

Incoming messages are checked against event.source === iframe.contentWindow plus per-instance ids and a per-frame nonce (sandbox-frame.tsx, use-preview-messages.ts) and only set heights/outputs; verification-sidebar checks event.origin; outgoing data is the model's own code. The sandbox CSP does share the img-src https: gap (noted in candidate 1).

webapp-network-trust.hypothesis: Control plane-served system prompt / model requestParams / GenUI allowlist as a config-injection vector
webapp-network-trust.why_rejected: Unauthenticated beyond WebPKI and by design (models.ts:590-612); it is Tinfoil's own position, so it is recorded as an attacker position of candidate 1 rather than a separate finding.

webapp-network-trust.hypothesis: Document upload endpoint from control-plane config could redirect uploads to a non-enclave host
webapp-network-trust.why_rejected: Uploads go through secureClient.fetch whose allowedOrigins guard (encrypted-body-fetch.ts:272-294) refuses any origin other than the attested enclave/base URL, and the body is sealed.

python-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: TLS pin checked after request bytes are sent (sync wrap_socket / async wrap_bio / urllib handler)
python-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: client.py _create_socket_wrapper wraps+handshakes then checks the SPKI fingerprint before returning the socket to httpcore; _create_bio_wrapper hooks SSLObject.do_handshake; TLSBoundHTTPSHandler checks right after connect(); re-verify retry only triggers on handshake-time cert/pin errors. No pre-pin send path.

python-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: EHBP Python client accepts unauthenticated 2xx responses / Python analogue of Go 3xx+303 forgery
python-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: ehbp/_http.py response_nonce_for_status fails closed for 2xx without Ehbp-Response-Nonce; only non-2xx pass through, httpx clients are built with follow_redirects=False and openai-python raises on 3xx, so no completion forgery. Bodyless (GET) plaintext pass-through is spec section 7.4 by design.

python-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: EHBP streaming truncation at a frame boundary (gateway delivers a well-formed prefix)
python-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: FrameDecryptor.finish only detects partial frames; SPEC 4.3/5.x explicitly treats a released prefix as authentic and relies on transport-level abort. Cross-SDK design limitation (integrity only, no injection: per-chunk seq nonces prevent reorder/replay); another hunter already targets it for Rust. Not pursued.

python-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: SEV-SNP: VCEK/ASK/ARK chain, report parsing, signature (R||S little-endian), policy/debug/SMT/platform-info, TCB checks
python-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: Pinned real AMD Genoa ARK/ASK, pyOpenSSL store verification, RSASSA-PSS/P-384 checks, HWID==CHIP_ID, VCEK TCB == reported_tcb, debug/migrate_ma rejected, mbz checks mirror go-sev-guest; VCEK cache content is re-verified against the chain so poisoning gains nothing. VMPL unchecked but not externally exploitable.

python-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: TDX quote signature/QE binding/PCK chain parsing weaknesses
python-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: Signature over raw[0:0x278] with the AK, QE report signed by PCK leaf, report_data == SHA256(AK||auth_data)||0, chain exactly 3 certs rooted at the pinned Intel root with CA checks and validity; only type-6 cert data; header version/AK type/TEE type/QE vendor enforced. QE identity MRSIGNER/ISVPRODID/attributes/miscselect/ISVSVN enforced (modulo the collateral differential).

python-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: Sigstore identity matching too loose (fork/other repo/other ref)
python-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: sigstore-python 4.5.0 GitHubWorkflowRepository is an exact string compare on the Fulcio repository extension; ref pattern is ^refs/tags/<escaped tag>\Z; issuer V2-preferred; legacy bundle layout, duplicate SCT logs and unknown in-toto fields rejected; subject digest compared exactly. Only an insider with push/tag rights to tinfoilsh/<repo> could mint a passing cert.

python-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: Bundle mode lets the bundle server pick domain/digest/releaseTag (rollback to an older signed release)
python-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: Any historical signed release of the configured repo passes, but exploiting it needs an old release with an exploitable bug and a genuine enclave running it; inherent to the bundle design and Tinfoil-side position. Not a crisp finding.

python-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: On-disk caches (VCEK, sigstore bundle, TDX collateral, user_cache_secret): poisoning, symlinks, permissions
python-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: All cached material is re-verified on load (VCEK chain, sigstore, collateral signature); cache dir is user-private (0700 for TDX, 0755 otherwise) and writing it requires running as the victim user; user_cache_secret uses O_NOFOLLOW/mkstemp/link and is injected into the body before sealing. No privilege boundary crossed.

python-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: DEFAULT_MIN_TCB_EVALUATION_DATA_NUMBER=19 hard-coded in the PCS request lets stale TCB evaluations be served
python-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: Intel PCS now answers 410 Gone for tcbEvaluationDataNumber=19 (TCB Info and QE Identity), so the pinned request fails closed (availability issue, not a bypass); an attacker who can serve old edition-19 collateral could forge arbitrary collateral anyway via the signature differential. Recorded in /root/tinfoil-review/work/python-sdk-verifier/intel-pcs/NOTES.txt.

python-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: github.py digest fallback (tinfoil.hash body unconstrained) enables cache-path traversal
python-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: Path is bundle_<repo>_<digest>.json under the cache dir; '..' would need a non-existent directory component, and the digest must still match the Sigstore subject. Attacker is Tinfoil's github-proxy anyway.

python-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: Pinned-measurement mode compares only registers[0] (MRTD for TDX) and skips RTMR/hardware checks
python-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: Requires a genuine TDX quote whose MRTD equals the pinned 48-byte SNP launch digest; infeasible.

python-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: KeyConfigMismatch (422) re-verification can be abused by the gateway
python-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: Forces a re-attest and a re-encrypted retry only; no plaintext replay (httpx HTTP/1.1, no body replay) and the new key must pass full attestation.

cvmimage-boot-config.hypothesis: The removed `cvm-source` runtime-source override (tinfoil-config <= v0.1.15, still consumed by measure-image-action HEAD which pins tinfoil-config v0.1.14) let the host swap the CVM runtime image.
cvmimage-boot-config.why_rejected: `cvm-source` lives in the MEASURED config (deployer-controlled, hashed into the cmdline). measure-image-action (internal/orchestrator/orchestrator.go:160-200) fetches the manifest from the named repo and requires a GitHub build-provenance attestation for that repo (`gh attestation verify -R <repo> --deny-self-hosted-runners`); kernel/initrd are checked against the manifest digests. The host never influences it; a malicious deployer could already ship a malicious container. Only an auditability footgun (now removed at tinfoil-config HEAD 043b28e); confidential-sandbox-gpu legitimately uses it for tinfoilsh/cvmimage-sandbox.

cvmimage-boot-config.hypothesis: Host enables debug mode (`tinfoil-debug=on`, debug toolbox with docker socket, host-supplied secrets despite keyserver-url, /v1/boot config-override API) while the VM still attests as the production release.
cvmimage-boot-config.why_rejected: pid1 reads the flag only from /proc/cmdline (internal/kernelcmdline/cmdline.go). The cmdline is part of the launch measurement on both platforms: measure-image-action emits a fixed cmdline without the flag (orchestrator.go:198) into sev-snp-measure --append (SNP launch digest) and tdx-measure (RTMR2: tdx-measure-tinfoil src/kernel.rs:136-140 hashes the UTF-16 cmdline), and tinfoil-go's verifier compares the launch digest / RTMR1+RTMR2 from the Sigstore-attested deployment plus MRTD/RTMR0/RTMR3==0 from platform endorsements, and enforces SNP guest policy DEBUG and TDX TD attributes from policies.json. The keyserver README also states debug attestations are rejected. No way to flip debug without changing the measurement.

cvmimage-boot-config.hypothesis: Kernel-cmdline parsing differential: initrd rejects duplicate roothash= while pid1 takes the FIRST tinfoil-config-hash=; a crafted cmdline could make the guest use a different config hash than the one the verifier expects.
cvmimage-boot-config.why_rejected: The whole cmdline string is measured (see above) and measure-image-action emits exactly one tinfoil-config-hash=; the verifier never parses the cmdline, it compares register values. Only the (private) tinfoild builds the cmdline and any change alters the measurement.

cvmimage-boot-config.hypothesis: Config-disk / NUL-padding trick lets the host feed a config whose bytes hash to the measured value but decode differently.
cvmimage-boot-config.why_rejected: cmd/boot/config.go readDiskPayload trims at the first NUL and rejects any non-NUL byte after it; sha256 over the trimmed bytes must equal the measured hash (lowercase 64-hex enforced). Same bytes are then decoded by the same pinned tinfoil-config in boot, pid1 and tinfoil-containers.

cvmimage-boot-config.hypothesis: Host-supplied external config (env/secrets/metadata/network, 'tinfoil-ext-config' disk, unmeasured) lets the host inject code or read secrets in a genuine enclave.
cvmimage-boot-config.why_rejected: Probed with attacker-controlled YAML (work/cvmimage-boot-config/cvmimage/tinfoil/cmd/boot/zz_hostinput_probe_test.go, log logs/host-input-probes.log): only env NAMES listed in the measured config reach a container (buildEnv), unlisted names like LD_PRELOAD are ignored; declared secrets come from the host only when keyserver-url is unset (documented design) and are REFUSED in keyserver mode (prepareSecretHandoff, cmd/boot/secrets.go:37-41); infra secrets (REGISTRY_*_TOKEN, GCLOUD_*, ECR_REGISTRY_AUTH, CERT_AUTH_TOKEN, CLOUDFLARE_*, METRICS_API_KEY) are host-owned by design; network values are netip-validated before `ip` invocation; metadata.repo/tag only steer collateral/keyserver requests. In all shipped tinfoil-config.yml files the only host-sourced env name is DOMAIN.

cvmimage-boot-config.hypothesis: Host sets env.DOMAIN=localhost to downgrade the enclave.
cvmimage-boot-config.why_rejected: Accepted (test above): generateIdentity accepts 'localhost' even with dummy-attestation:false, and cmd/boot/cpuattest.go:31 then emits a non-cryptographic 'dummy' V2 document while cert.go:93 issues a self-signed cert; with keyserver secrets declared the boot fails closed (prefetchKeyserverCollateral rejects platform dummy). v3 attestation still carries a genuine hardware quote (no collateral), models stay verity-verified and secrets are not exposed; clients using the dummy V2 doc fail closed. Availability/degradation only (excluded by the brief). Hardening suggestion: reject DOMAIN=localhost unless dummy-attestation is measured.

cvmimage-boot-config.hypothesis: Container image pulling: tag-only refs, registry MITM, or host-supplied registry credentials let the host run an unmeasured image.
cvmimage-boot-config.why_rejected: tinfoil-config validateContainerImage requires a digested reference; tinfoil-containers verifyPulledImageDigest (internal/containers/containers.go) checks RepoDigests after ImagePull and Docker verifies manifest/layer digests, so a MITM or wrong credential can only cause failure. Boot writes only an `auths` map (no credsStore/credHelpers) into the private docker config, so docker/cli cannot be made to exec helpers. The 2026-10-06 ECR refresh (internal/ecrregistry) uses a host-owned token over WebPKI to api.tinfoil.sh with redirects refused and strict response validation; nothing to gain.

cvmimage-boot-config.hypothesis: Model packs (MWP/EMWP) mounted from host-supplied disks could be substituted.
cvmimage-boot-config.why_rejected: Root hash, hash offset and the dm-verity salt (SHA256 of the measured `repo` string, modelwrap.VeritySalt) all come from the measured config; geometry is derived from the measured hash offset, never from the untrusted superblock (cmd/boot/models.go verityTable); EMWP decrypts (aes-xts, HKDF-derived key) underneath verity so a wrong key or tampering fails closed; encrypted models require explicit container grants (validateModelAccess).

cvmimage-boot-config.hypothesis: Persistent volumes: argon2id key stretching (#375), unjournaled dm-integrity (#409), 'reject writes while locked' (#378) or uid:gid ownership (#413) introduce a host-exploitable weakness.
cvmimage-boot-config.why_rejected: Read all four diffs. Stack is dm-integrity (tag store, mode D) + dm-crypt capi:authenc(hmac(sha256),xts(aes))-random with 48-byte tags; the header salt is host-controlled but the key is secret; a wrong key or tampered sector reads back as EIO (mount fails, no silent reformat); blank-disk detection only enables a fresh format (data loss, not disclosure); the legacy format-1 path is reachable only by the owning container and cannot initialize. The sole host capability is whole-volume or per-sector rollback (no freshness is claimed anywhere in docs); could not PoC here because the WSL2 kernel lacks CONFIG_DM_INTEGRITY, and it would be a known design limitation rather than a bug.

cvmimage-boot-config.hypothesis: Secrets handoff from boot to tinfoil-containers can be tampered with or read by other services.
cvmimage-boot-config.why_rejected: internal/secretstore uses a sealed memfd (F_SEAL_SEAL|SHRINK|GROW|WRITE) passed as an fd, bound to the sha256 of the verified config and the exact set of declared names; keyserver-fetched values never touch disk (external-config.yml is written before the merge).

cvmimage-boot-config.hypothesis: Host chooses metadata.repo to make the enclave fetch another tenant's keyserver secrets.
cvmimage-boot-config.why_rejected: Keyserver (repos/keyserver) authenticates the attestation document against the Sigstore identity of the requested repo, pins repo+tag per workload and additionally pins a domain bound to the enclave's CA-issued mTLS certificate; a matching enclave is a genuine instance of that tenant's own code, so the host gains nothing it cannot get by launching that deployment itself.

cvmimage-boot-config.hypothesis: Validator drift: measure-image-action pins tinfoil-config v0.1.14 while cvmimage HEAD pins v0.1.15 (volumes: vs persistent_volumes:, owner int->string), so a measured, attested release may be interpreted differently or fail at boot.
cvmimage-boot-config.why_rejected: Reproduced (work/cvmimage-boot-config/poc-validator-drift/repro.sh, logs/validator-drift.log): confidential-ubuntu-config, confidential-ubuntu-tinfoil-config and confidential-agent-sandbox validate under v0.1.14 but are rejected by v0.1.15 ('names persistent volume ... mount it with persistent_volumes'). The guest fails closed (boot error), the semantics never widen, and the affected repos pin older cvm-versions; availability/compat only, not security.

cvmimage-boot-config.hypothesis: Shim path allowlist / authenticated-endpoints matching can be bypassed (e.g. encoded or dotted paths) to reach an authenticated endpoint without an API key.
cvmimage-boot-config.why_rejected: Skimmed only (likely another hunter's area): matching is on the ServeMux-cleaned URL.Path with segment-boundary wildcard logic and is covered by api_path_test.go; CONNECT tunnels always require a key when a validator exists and fail closed when `authenticated` is set without a validator.

cvmimage-boot-config.hypothesis: Host attaches extra/mis-ordered virtio devices to confuse disk selection.
cvmimage-boot-config.why_rejected: internal/device/topology.go pins each role to a fixed PCI slot, virtio-blk vendor/device IDs and a fixed serial string; mismatches fail; extra devices are ignored.

sync-and-storage.hypothesis: Clerk JWT verification weaknesses (alg none/confusion, issuer/audience/expiry, kid-driven JWKS)
sync-and-storage.why_rejected: internal/auth/jwt.go pins RS/ES methods, keyfunc returns typed public keys (HS with RSA bytes rejected, smoke T11), exp required with 30s leeway, iss checked twice, kid refresh rate-limited; audience is intentionally unenforced (Clerk tokens omit aud) which adds nothing since the operator can mint JWTs anyway and the CEK is the real secret.

sync-and-storage.hypothesis: Path traversal / encoding tricks in sidecar object keys to escape the per-user tenant prefix
sync-and-storage.why_rejected: Empirically tested against the real sidecar jar + moto (tools/sidecar_probe_output.txt): tenant prefix is prepended server-side, Jetty/Javalin pass dot segments literally into the key and S3 stores 'user-B/x/../../user-A/att1' verbatim; cross-tenant GET -> NoSuchKey; tenant header regex rejects '/', '..', '%2F'.

sync-and-storage.hypothesis: Another authenticated user reading/overwriting a victim's attachment through fork/legacy-promotion/import attachment ids taken from attacker-controlled chat JSON
sync-and-storage.why_rejected: Every such buckets call uses the caller's own tenant (sess.Claims.Subject); AttachmentDelete requires the CP ownership delete first; native import re-mints ids via AttachmentPut and rejects unsafe archive paths; the only session-agnostic read (get/get-public) needs the 256-bit per-attachment key.

sync-and-storage.hypothesis: Legacy-attachment promotion (rewrap.go promoteOneAttachment) lets a share recipient hijack the owner's attachment index row
sync-and-storage.why_rejected: Requires three unverifiable controlplane behaviours (public legacy /api/storage/attachment/:id, claim stamped for the requesting user, upsert of attachment-index owner); the enclave verifies the CP's HMAC claim for (sub, id, sha256) so only the CP could enable it; left unproven.

sync-and-storage.hypothesis: Search index cache / search objects leak another user's or JWT-only data
sync-and-storage.why_rejected: Cache keyed by owner and sha256(HKDF(CEK)||objectKey); index object sealed under HKDF(CEK); query responses carry chat ids and scores only; object keys are random per publication.

sync-and-storage.hypothesis: Import staging chunks readable by the operator in S3
sync-and-storage.why_rejected: Staging key is a random in-memory per-job key (import_jobs.go:321), zeroed on completion, chunks deleted after the job.

sync-and-storage.hypothesis: Controlplane URL/path/header injection via user-chosen scope/id/idempotency/project ids
sync-and-storage.why_rejected: All ids pass url.PathEscape (project_document split on first '/'), Go's net/http refuses invalid header values, op-hash binds the exact path; nothing reaches a different CP route.

sync-and-storage.hypothesis: Envelope cross-user/cross-id/cross-scope blob swapping by a malicious controlplane
sync-and-storage.why_rejected: v2 AAD binds clerk_user_id, scope, id and kid (smoke T03-T05); legacy v0/v1 blobs lack AAD but still need the user's CEK.
Fresh random 256-bit key per share, key only in URL fragment, /v1/share/open only decrypts attacker-supplied ciphertext with attacker-supplied key.

sync-and-storage.hypothesis: Embedding egress (chat text to the embedding model) via tinfoil-go v0.13.3 / EHBP v0.2.5 default EHBP transport
sync-and-storage.why_rejected: Already covered by known Finding 1 (older-variant note names confidential-sync); not re-reported.

sync-and-storage.hypothesis: confidential-secret-storage / confidential-debug-secret-consumer: shim exposes unauthenticated /upload_key, /store, /push and /receive (anyone can overwrite any user's key, SSRF-ish /push of all keys to an attested host)
sync-and-storage.why_rejected: Demo repos (db-demo-storage, 'debug' consumer); key overwrite is only DoS/integrity, /push only delivers keys to a host passing attestation for the consumer repo whose verbatim code never exposes keys; brief excludes examples/demos.
Example only; single-tenant sidecar with an operator-held ENCRYPTION_KEY by design.

sync-and-storage.hypothesis: Sidecar reachable from the host/internet (port 9000) as a decrypt/delete oracle
sync-and-storage.why_rejected: cvmimage containernet publishes only the shim (443 -> upstream-port) and binds operator ports to 127.0.0.1 inside the CVM; and the sidecar still needs per-object keys.

sync-and-storage.hypothesis: In-memory migration/import/reindex coordinators leak state across users
sync-and-storage.why_rejected: All keyed by the verified JWT subject; status endpoints return counts/ids for the caller only.

webapp-sandbox-bridge.hypothesis: Nested artifact/preview document forges tinfoil-sandbox-ready or speaks for another preview (instanceId/nonce/source spoofing)
webapp-sandbox-bridge.why_rejected: preview.js relays nested messages only with the current run's instanceId and the chat checks event.source === iframe.contentWindow plus a crypto.randomUUID nonce carried in the URL fragment, which the opaque-origin nested doc cannot read (cross-origin location, referrerpolicy=no-referrer, fragments never in Referer); readyRef also stops re-posting; the artifact kind has no chat-side listener at all.

webapp-sandbox-bridge.hypothesis: Relayed preview messages drive an HTML/navigation sink in the chat
webapp-sandbox-bridge.why_rejected: html-preview-height is Number-checked and clamped to 100..2000 (code-block.tsx:265-271), js/python output must pass isPreviewOutput and is rendered as text nodes, map-preview-status is enum-checked (MapView.tsx:148-155); no dangerouslySetInnerHTML or URL sink is reachable.

webapp-sandbox-bridge.hypothesis: url-type artifacts frame something dangerous (chat itself, verification center, sandbox /map)
webapp-sandbox-bridge.why_rejected: Chat CSP frame-src allows only 'self' + verification-center + the two sandbox hosts; the chat cannot frame itself because its own frame-ancestors lists only tinfoil.sh/www.tinfoil.sh; VC or /map framed with sandbox=allow-scripts get an opaque origin, so event.origin checks fail and /map holds no data (its MapKit token is origin-bound and not secret).

webapp-sandbox-bridge.hypothesis: /map allow-same-origin frame exposes sandbox-origin state or can be driven by other tinfoil.sh pages
webapp-sandbox-bridge.why_rejected: frame-ancestors is https://*.tinfoil.sh but the origin stores nothing, run messages are accepted only from window.parent with kind 'map', CHAT_ORIGIN is learned from the first run, and status messages are an enum; no tinfoil.sh subdomain serving attacker HTML was identified.

webapp-sandbox-bridge.hypothesis: Verification sidebar can be driven to show 'verified' for a fake document
webapp-sandbox-bridge.why_rejected: verification-sidebar.tsx:145 accepts only origin https://verification-center.tinfoil.sh and the chat fetches/posts its own document; the badge comes from tinfoil-client, not the iframe. The verification-center page itself (app/page.tsx:20-26) accepts TINFOIL_VERIFICATION_DOCUMENT from any origin and its CSP (webcat/vercel.config.json) has no frame-ancestors, so any site can embed the real VC and display 'Security verified' for a fabricated document; recorded as a low-value UI-spoof hardening note, not a candidate.

webapp-sandbox-bridge.hypothesis: CSP `sandbox` directive vs iframe attribute mismatch grants popups/forms/same-origin to artifacts
webapp-sandbox-bridge.why_rejected: Flags intersect (restrictions union); ArtifactPreview.tsx:257 now sets only allow-scripts anyway; /preview opened top-level is confirmed opaque by the header in the repo's own smoke test; no path serves preview.html under the /map (allow-same-origin) header block.

webapp-sandbox-bridge.hypothesis: RecipeCard 'Print' popup is an HTML injection sink in the chat origin
webapp-sandbox-bridge.why_rejected: window.open('', '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer') returns null in modern browsers so document.write is never reached, and the generated HTML escapes every model field.

webapp-sandbox-bridge.hypothesis: SVG/Mermaid in-origin previews leak or inject
webapp-sandbox-bridge.why_rejected: SVG goes through DOMPurify (svg profile) into a data: ; Mermaid runs with securityLevel strict, htmlLabels false, script-src 'self' only in a sandboxed frame.

webapp-sandbox-bridge.hypothesis: Focus forwarding (window focus -> nested doc, onMouseEnter autofocus in the artifact sidebar) enables keylogging
webapp-sandbox-bridge.why_rejected: Only keystrokes while the artifact is focused are observable; the chat composer visibly loses focus; sandboxed opaque frame cannot read clipboard (no allow attribute, cross-origin permissions policy); low value.

webapp-sandbox-bridge.hypothesis: Forced ?q= prompt on / exposes harness memory or the last conversation
webapp-sandbox-bridge.why_rejected: The webapp talks to the model router directly (/v1/chat/completions), project memory is disabled in the webapp (use-chat-messaging.ts:1150) and / opens a blank chat, so only personalization/custom instructions are in context; chat/project ids are UUIDs not leaked via referrer.

webapp-sandbox-bridge.hypothesis: Verification document posted into the VC iframe contains secrets
webapp-sandbox-bridge.why_rejected: It is the public attestation document (measurements, fingerprints, public keys, step statuses); nothing user-specific.

cvmimage-shim-api.hypothesis: Path-normalization differential: shim checks the decoded r.URL.Path (allowlist + authenticated-endpoints) but httputil.ReverseProxy forwards the raw EscapedPath, so percent-encoded dot segments (/v1/%2E%2E/agui, /v1/..%2Fagui, /v1%2F..%2Fmetrics) pass as unauthenticated '/v1/*' and reach the upstream verbatim (reproduced on the handler and on the built binary: poc/probe1.log, poc/e2e-probe.log).
cvmimage-shim-api.why_rejected: Only matters with wildcard allowlists (confidential-tinfoil-harness '/v1/*' protecting /agui; confidential-model-router '/v1/*','/' protecting /metrics). Both upstreams are Go: harness uses http.ServeMux patterns (api.go:151-190) which never resolves %2E%2E, model-router compares r.URL.Path literally (main.go:641-665). All vLLM-style deployments use exact-match allowlists, where the decoded path must equal '/v1/models' or '/health' exactly, leaving no raw/decoded gap (uvicorn/Starlette do not normalize dot segments either). Literal '..', '//' and '/./' are 307-redirected by Go 1.27 ServeMux before the handler (cmd/shim/api.go:294). No shipped upstream turns this into an auth bypass; hardening note only.

cvmimage-shim-api.hypothesis: Other path-class bypasses: trailing slash, ';' params, %00, %20, case, '#', absolute-form targets, HTTP/2 :path tricks, extended CONNECT with :path.
cvmimage-shim-api.why_rejected: All return 404/401 or redirect (probe1.log). requiresAuth and pathAllowed (api.go:48-86) use the same decoded path, so they cannot disagree with each other; Go 1.27.1 disables extended CONNECT by default (net/http/internal/http2/http2.go:44), so CONNECT never carries a path and is always keyed by authorize() (api.go:246-248).

cvmimage-shim-api.hypothesis: HTTP/2 CONNECT tunnel reaches arbitrary host loopback services or bypasses the allowlist.
cvmimage-shim-api.why_rejected: tunnels() (cmd/shim/tunnel.go:50-100) only dials 127.0.0.1:<port> for ports declared in runtime-config 'ports:'; tinfoil-config validation rejects 443/80/2222; authorize() requires a validated key whenever a validator exists and NewShimServer nils the target set when authenticated:true has no validator (api.go:305-307). Unkeyed CONNECT (401) reproduced in TestProbeH2.

cvmimage-shim-api.hypothesis: Unkeyed CONNECT tunnel on authenticated:false deployments exposes every published loopback port (agent sandbox: 22, 3000-9222, 5900, 3389, 3306, 5432, 6379) to anyone who knows the domain.
cvmimage-shim-api.why_rejected: Real exposure but explicitly acknowledged in the measured config (confidential-agent-sandbox/tinfoil-config.yml comments: 'answers to anyone who knows the domain'); sshd is key-bound; impact depends entirely on what the user binds. Documented design, not a code defect; not reported.

cvmimage-shim-api.hypothesis: Local attestation socket lets a workload container obtain a quote over attacker-chosen REPORT_DATA and impersonate the enclave.
cvmimage-shim-api.why_rejected: newLocalAttestationHandler (attestation_socket.go:176-201) only admits GET on the three attestation paths with exactly one 64-hex nonce and no body; REPORT_DATA = SHA256(alg||nonce||H(crypto_material)||H(device_evidence)) with zeroed upper 32 bytes (tinfoil-go document.go:296-309), so neither half is controllable; the crypto_material section is the shim's own TLS/HPKE/workload keys. Socket is bind-mounted only for 'attestation: true' containers (containers.go:497-499) and the doc states a quote does not identify the requester.

cvmimage-shim-api.hypothesis: Workload containers can reach the shim/host (metadata, docker, private ramdisk) over the bridge.
cvmimage-shim-api.why_rejected: Measured /etc/nftables.conf has input/forward policy drop; firewall/containers.go:113 adds 'container_input iifname <bridge> ct state new drop' for every bridge incl. implicit shim-net; egress rules drop RFC1918/link-local; docker daemon.json has icc=false, ipv6 off. Private ramdisk is 0700 and only /mnt/ramdisk/public is bind-mounted (/tinfoil:ro).

cvmimage-shim-api.hypothesis: TLS/HPKE private key custody: key files world-readable or reachable from containers; signing/decryption oracle.
cvmimage-shim-api.why_rejected: Keys are written 0600 under the 0700 private tmpfs by tinfoil-boot (cert.go:450-474, identity.go:275-291); the shim runs with only CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE, no-new-privs, seccomp and restricted filesystem view (pid1/hardening/hardening.go:148-154). The only HPKE use is EHBP request decryption plus response encryption bound to the requester's encapsulated key; /.well-known/hpke-keys serves public config only (ConfigHandler). HPKE file race between shim and boot impossible: shim waits for the TLS cert (boot step 6) before loading the HPKE key (boot step 3).

cvmimage-shim-api.hypothesis: JWT validator weaknesses (alg confusion, missing aud/iss/exp, plain-HTTP JWKS, kid tricks).
cvmimage-shim-api.why_rejected: key/jwt/jwt.go: ParseSigned restricted to EdDSA, typ must be at+jwt, kid looked up in JWKS fetched over HTTPS from the control-plane URL (online validator enforces https prefix), claims.Validate checks iss, aud, exp/nbf/iat, requires sub/jti/client_id and inference:api scope; /metrics forced to online validation. No defect found. Local JWT path skipping per-request quota/host/path policy is by design and unverifiable without the private control plane.

cvmimage-shim-api.hypothesis: Cert-proxy/ACME flow lets the control plane or host install a cert for a different key or expose port 80/443 handlers.
cvmimage-shim-api.why_rejected: tls.X509KeyPair verifies the returned cert against the enclave-generated P-384 key (certproxy.go:127); HTTP-01 server serves only /.well-known/acme-challenge/<token> while nft http01 chain is open and is closed afterwards (cert.go:476-491). Clients pin the key fingerprint from attestation, so the cert's name content is not security relevant.

cvmimage-shim-api.hypothesis: Reverse-proxy header tricks: Connection header stripping Director-set Forwarded/X-Forwarded-Host, XFF spoofing against the harness, Host injection into Forwarded.
cvmimage-shim-api.why_rejected: Reproduced that 'Connection: X-Forwarded-Host, Forwarded' strips those headers (HTTP/1.1 only), but X-Forwarded-For is re-added with the real client IP after hop-by-hop removal; the harness uses rightmost-untrusted XFF (auth.go:120-140) and nothing routes on X-Forwarded-Host. Go validates Host so no quote/CRLF injection into the Forwarded header.

cvmimage-shim-api.hypothesis: expected-gpus defaulting to 0 would omit GPU evidence from fresh v3 documents.
cvmimage-shim-api.why_rejected: tinfoil-config/decode.go:34 copies the top-level gpus count into ShimConfig.ExpectedGPUs; CollectDeviceEvidence enforces the exact count (gpu.go:233-245).

cvmimage-shim-api.hypothesis: Host-supplied external config (DOMAIN, secrets, metadata) subverts the shim.
cvmimage-shim-api.why_rejected: Only used as control-plane policy inputs, metrics labels, ACME/registry credentials and (when no keyserver-url) container secrets; secrets.go:301-304 refuses host values for declared secrets when a keyserver is configured. All by documented design (external config is unmeasured and untrusted).

cvmimage-shim-api.hypothesis: Volume control socket or secret handoff reachable by the wrong container.
cvmimage-shim-api.why_rejected: volume/worker.go: socket 0600 owned by the volume owner uid, initialize only on a blank device, unlock needs the key; only containers that mount the volume get the bind. Secret handoff is a sealed fd between pid1/boot/containers.

rust-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: TLS pin checked only after the request is sent (summarizer-style bug) in tinfoil-rs
rust-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: The pin is enforced inside rustls `PinnedCertVerifier::verify_server_cert` (src/verifier/tls.rs:80-117, WebPKI chain then SPKI pin) during the handshake; `verify_tls_binding` (client.rs:398-516) only does a bare TLS handshake and inspects the cert. Loopback control (results/tls_pin_order_evidence.txt): with a correct pin but untrusted chain, and with a wrong pin, the server sees `received fatal alert: CertificateUnknown`, handshake never completes, 0 application bytes (Authorization never sent).

All 54 tinfoil-conformance sigstore vectors run through the shipped checks (results/sigstore_vectors.md). Every reject-expected vector is rejected except (a) policy-configuration vectors 010/011/013/014/015/051/052 whose policy differs from Rust's hard-coded production policy (harness artifact) and (b) 060b/070, where Rust checks BuildSignerURI (1.9, job_workflow_ref) instead of GitHubWorkflowRef/SourceRepositoryRef (1.6/1.14) - a divergence the conformance repo already documents as 'old Rust behavior' (vector 071 notes); exploiting it needs a tag-pinned reusable-workflow run inside the Tinfoil repo itself (repo write access); the real release workflows (confidential-model-router tinfoil-release*.yml) have no such call. Rekor entry binds cert, signature and payload hash; Merkle proof + checkpoint signature verified; Fulcio chain walked to the self-signed root with signature checks; SCTs verified.

rust-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: Rekor integratedTime is unauthenticated because the SET (inclusionPromise) is never verified
rust-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: True (rekor.rs:47-65 trusts the bundle's integratedTime; only the checkpoint/inclusion proof is checked) and already known to Tinfoil (fixturegen/lib/rekor.py:132 comment). Abuse requires a leaked ephemeral Fulcio key from Tinfoil CI plus a real Rekor inclusion proof; no outsider path. Not reported.

49 attestation-sev vectors through `sev::verify_full_with_options` with injected VCEK/chain (results/sev_vectors.md): all reject-expected vectors rejected except 240 (vector pins a future check date; shipped code uses the system clock and the real VCEK is valid today) and 430/440 (id/author key digest pins that Rust's ValidationOptions do not model and production never sets). ARK SPKI pinned, RSA-PSS chain, P-384 report signature over bytes 0..672, MBZ/signer-info/TCB/platform/VMPL checks, VCEK extension and HWID match all enforced.

rust-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: Go-style plaintext body replay on HTTP/2 REFUSED_STREAM/GOAWAY in the Rust EHBP client
rust-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: tinfoil-ehbp rust/src/client.rs:209-268 replaces the body with `reqwest::Body::wrap_stream` (non-reusable) and encrypts lazily inside the stream; reqwest only retries reusable `Bytes` bodies and hyper-util only re-sends requests that never left the dispatch channel (body unpolled, still ciphertext). Confirms the report's 'not affected' note.

rust-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: Forged/unauthenticated responses accepted in Rust proxy mode (analog of Go Finding 4)
rust-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: Nonce-less 2xx fails closed (tinfoil-ehbp client.rs:313-318); nonce-less non-2xx (incl. 3xx) is passed through but both consumers error on non-2xx (async-openai `execute_response` `is_success`; relaxed.rs:55 `http_error`); the proxy reqwest client has `redirect::Policy::none()` (ehbp_transport.rs:106-108); bodyless authenticated requests are refused before transmission. Only truncation remains (reported).

rust-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: 422 key-config mismatch lets the proxy re-key the client to an attacker key
rust-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: `refresh_after_mismatch` (ehbp_transport.rs:223-261) re-runs the full attestation chain (`verify_rotated_state` -> sigstore + SEV + TLS binding) and refuses a previously rejected key; only a genuinely attested enclave key can be installed.

rust-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: Router discovery (atc.tinfoil.sh) / github-proxy / kds-proxy as unauthenticated inputs leak secrets or bypass verification
rust-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: Those fetches carry no secrets (SDK identity headers only); the API key is only sent through the pinned client after verification or to the proxy by design. A WebPKI-capable MITM can at most relay to another genuine enclave running the verified code or cause DoS. Release rollback via github-proxy needs a still-deployed older enclave and ATC cooperation (Tinfoil-internal, common to all SDKs; Rust also has no V3/freshness flow).

rust-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: V3 document / TDX collateral differentials in tinfoil-rs
rust-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: tinfoil-rs has no V3 document flow and returns `UnsupportedFormat` for TDX (attestation/mod.rs:100-111); the hypotheses do not apply to this SDK.

rust-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: x509 parse/re-encode differential between Fulcio identity extraction and signature verification
rust-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: fulcio.rs:141-145 re-encodes the parsed TBS for signature verification, so any non-canonical input that changed the parsed extensions would fail the signature (fail closed).

rust-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: SAN `.hatt.`/`.hpke.` dcode parsing or multi-platform measurement comparison bypass
rust-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: decode_from_sans rejects duplicate indices and malformed chunks; the hash is sha256(format_url||body) as in Go/JS; compare_multiplatform checks register[0] against the SEV measurement (string-exact lowercase hex). No bypass without the enclave's TLS key.

go-verifier-quotes.hypothesis: Tinfoil's go-sev-guest fork weakens SEV-SNP checks (diffed against google/go-sev-guest v0.15.0)
go-verifier-quotes.why_rejected: Diff only adds Turin TCB layout/FMC SPL, 8-byte HWID binding (report CHIP_ID[:8] vs cert, still signed), PLATFORM_INFO bit 6 as IOMMUWriteSafe (tinfoil-go compares PLATFORM_INFO by strict equality), TCB-format consistency checks. No relaxed check found.

go-verifier-quotes.hypothesis: Document-supplied ASK/ARK cert_chain_pem or amd-crl could substitute the AMD trust anchor
go-verifier-quotes.why_rejected: decodeCerts verifies the VCEK only against options.TrustedRoots (embedded Genoa/Turin ASK+ARK); the document chain is ignored for trust; CRL must be ARK-signed and inside [ThisUpdate,NextUpdate]; wrong product line fails CN/ARK checks.

go-verifier-quotes.hypothesis: SEV report re-serialization (ReportToProto/ReportToAbiBytes) or SignerInfo/VLEK/NONE signer kinds let an unsigned field be validated
go-verifier-quotes.why_rejected: MBZ fields enforced, signature verified over the re-serialized proto, VLEK without cert and NONE signer fail closed, MaskChipKey rejected, ID-block/author-key reports rejected.

go-verifier-quotes.hypothesis: Exact duplicate JSON keys (the tinfoil-python mechanism) in Go collateral or in tinfoil-go's own JSON (document, collateral, policy artifact, recorder)
go-verifier-quotes.why_rejected: go-tdx-guest: last-wins applies to both struct and raw map, so the forged copy fails the Intel signature (control test). tinfoil-go uses encoding/json/v2 with RejectUnknownMembers, duplicate names rejected, case-sensitive: no differential.

go-verifier-quotes.hypothesis: REPORT_DATA / nonce binding or endorsed-section hashing can be bypassed
go-verifier-quotes.why_rejected: Parse recomputes SHA-256 over the exact base64-decoded section bytes and the full 64-byte REPORT_DATA is compared verbatim on both platforms; nonce equality enforced; Assemble requires the same evidence bytes that were authenticated.

go-verifier-quotes.hypothesis: Sigstore provenance identity/digest/freshness checks are weaker than intended (workflow regex, tag ref, subject[0], SCT dedup, legacy bundle, witness time)
go-verifier-quotes.why_rejected: SAN regex anchored and repo escaped, refs/tags/ required and tag matched, subject[0] digest enforced, duplicate-SCT and legacy-layout rejected, exactly one DSSE signature, witness bound to repo/tag/commit/subject and Tlog time with 7-day bound. Rollback to an older still-witnessed release is by design and depends on the control plane (freshness-witness only witnesses what the control plane requests; not verifiable from code).

go-verifier-quotes.hypothesis: Multi-platform measurement/shape resolution lets a wrong-shape or GPU-less VM pass as a GPU shape
go-verifier-quotes.why_rejected: Shape (cpus/memory/disks) must match; GPUs compared only when the measurement declares it, but RTMR0 differs per GPU topology in the endorsed artifact, so a different topology cannot match.

go-verifier-quotes.hypothesis: TDX identity (PPID) extraction or quote structural checks can be confused (cert chain order, extra bytes, reserved bytes)
go-verifier-quotes.why_rejected: PPID is read from the same first PEM block go-tdx-guest verifies as the PCK leaf; extra/reserved bytes must be zero; QE report signature by PCK and attestation-key binding (SHA256(ak||authdata)) are checked, so a non-host attacker cannot forge quotes.

go-verifier-quotes.hypothesis: Transport binding (TLS pin, host-bound origins, mobile Verify) has a pre-data or origin bypass
go-verifier-quotes.why_rejected: Pin checked in tls.Config.VerifyConnection before any data; hostBoundTransport restricts origins; remaining EHBP issues are the known findings 1 and 4.

go-verifier-quotes.hypothesis: Platform-endorsements artifact v0.0.9 (frozen fixture) lacks iommu_write_safe for Turin so HEAD rejects Turin
go-verifier-quotes.why_rejected: Availability only; current platform-endorsements HEAD policies.json sets iommu_write_safe:true for amd-turin-prod.

js-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: Forge or mutate the SEV-SNP report / VCEK so the JS verifier accepts attacker report_data or measurement
js-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: Signature over 0x2A0 bytes with ECDSA P-384 under the VCEK, VCEK chained to hardcoded Genoa ASK/ARK (RSASSA-PSS SHA-384), HWID/TCB extension equality, CN/product-name/CSP_ID checks; every mutation (report_data, measurement, policy debug bit, signature, vmpl, host_data, chip_id masking, VLEK signer, ASK-as-VCEK) is rejected; all 49 conformance attestation-sev negatives that apply are rejected (harness/sev-mutations-output.txt, conformance-run.log). Only harmless trailing bytes after the 1184-byte report are tolerated.

js-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: Fulcio chain/SCT bypass in sigstore-browser (self-signed leaf, untrusted intermediate, DER re-encoding malleability, hash-algorithm confusion)
js-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: CertificateChainVerifier only accepts paths containing a trusted-root object (object identity), self-signed leaves are filtered out, intermediates must be CA, signature verified over re-encoded TBS with the issuer key and the cert's own ECDSA/RSA-PSS OID; parse is deterministic so re-encoding cannot change semantics; SCT verified against CT log keys with PreCert reconstruction. Conformance 091/092/065/066 rejected.

js-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: Policy bypass via GitHub Actions claims (fork PRs, pull_request_target, reusable workflows, renamed orgs, V1/V2 issuer disagreement 069b)
js-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: repository claim is the run's repo (forks give the fork name), pull_request_target yields refs/heads/*, workflow ref regex ^refs/tags/ is anchored, repo compared exactly; V1-only issuer check (069b) cannot diverge for genuine Fulcio certs since both extensions come from the same OIDC iss.

js-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: Legacy x509CertificateChain bundle layout smuggled past the tinfoil guard (snake_case key, both keys present)
js-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: Guard rejects any truthy x509CertificateChain; sigstore-browser reads only the camelCase key, so a snake_case chain yields 'No certificate found'.

js-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: Enclave certificate / dcode SAN binding (hpke, hatt, domain, wildcard) weaknesses
js-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: Cert is self-asserted by design (AGENTS.md); what matters is equality with report_data-derived HPKE key and sha256(format+body), both enforced; all 9 enclave-cert conformance vectors behave as expected. Domain substitution by the bundle server only redirects ciphertext.

js-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: compareMeasurements partial/case confusion, prototype pollution via in-toto JSON, unanchored regex
js-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: Strict string equality on registers[0] (lowercase hex both sides), unknown top-level in-toto fields rejected, no object merging, regex anchored.

js-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: EHBP response forgery / 3xx downgrade in the JS client (variant of known Finding 4)
js-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: ehbp 0.3.3 requires Ehbp-Response-Nonce for every 2xx of a body-carrying request and AEAD-decrypts chunks; redirect re-sends only ciphertext and the final response must still be encrypted; non-2xx pass-through only reaches openai-node error handling. Streamed-response truncation at a chunk boundary is silent but is integrity-only and is being covered by the Rust-SDK hunter.

js-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: TLS pinning ordering / WebSocket pinning bypass in Node
js-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: checkServerIdentity runs inside tls.connect before secureConnect; https.request does not follow redirects; ws options that could weaken the pin are stripped and Bun is refused.

js-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: Attacker runs the same measured Tinfoil image on own SNP hardware with a different workload (unmeasured host_data/config)
js-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: measure-image-action puts tinfoil-config-hash and roothash in the measured kernel cmdline, so the container config is inside the launch measurement; host_data is zero in production and unused; JS not checking host_data/vmpl/image_id is a divergence from Go V3 policy but not exploitable.

js-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: Rollback: bundle server serves an older signed release + matching old enclave
js-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: Accepted by design (no freshness/witness/endorsement layer in tinfoil-js, unlike Go V3), but exploitation needs a historically vulnerable release; speculative, no PoC.

js-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: Missing TSA/observer timestamp with a garbage RFC3161 timestamp and no integratedTime (variant I)
js-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: RFC3161 parse errors propagate ('request past end of buffer') and an empty list hits assertRekorV2Timestamp; only the unsigned-integratedTime route works.

js-sdk-verifier.hypothesis: Conformance DIVERGENCE-ACCEPTS on sigstore 010/011/013/014/015/051/052/078 and sev 400-461/450/451
js-sdk-verifier.why_rejected: Harness artifacts: those vectors change policy knobs (issuer, ref prefix, predicate/payload allow-lists, measurement/host_data pins, caller minimum TCB) that tinfoil-js hardcodes; with the shipped policy they are not bypasses. sev 265/270-274 (vmpl range, hardened platform-info bits) are strictness differences, not attacker-exploitable without own hardware.

webapp-keys-storage.hypothesis: CEK or plaintext shipped to a Tinfoil-controlled non-enclave server or third party (analytics, logs, Clerk metadata, query strings, raw fetch)
webapp-keys-storage.why_rejected: Every raw fetch() in src/ goes to api.tinfoil.sh with JWT only (ids, billing, share ciphertext, safeguard flags, model config); CEK/plaintext only travel inside SecureClient (EHBP) to attested enclaves (sync/router/summarizer/metadata). logError/logInfo are console-only (utils/error-handling.ts). Clerk unsafeMetadata holds only has_completed_onboarding; telemetry={false}. Vendored plausible.js sends origin+pathname only, excludes /, /chat*, /share*, /project/*/chat*, and tests/pages/plausible-analytics.test.ts pins this. No vitals/beacon/cookie/BroadcastChannel/window.name use.

webapp-keys-storage.hypothesis: KDF weakness: PRF->KEK derivation or CEK format allows low-entropy/deterministic keys
webapp-keys-storage.why_rejected: KEK = HKDF-SHA256(32-byte authenticator PRF output, info 'tinfoil-chat-kek-v1'); CEK = 256-bit AES-GCM key from crypto.subtle.generateKey; key_id = HKDF(CEK) 128-bit non-reversible; wrap = AES-GCM random 12-byte IV; bundle/record formats are strictly validated (passkey-kit crypto.ts/wrapped-key-record-codec.ts). Only a user can type an all-zero key manually.

webapp-keys-storage.hypothesis: Browser SecureClient falls back to plain TLS (no EHBP) when the attestation lacks an HPKE key, exposing the CEK sent in every sync request
webapp-keys-storage.why_rejected: tinfoil 1.2.2 secure-fetch.js:19-28 throws ConfigurationError in browsers without an HPKE key; pinned-tls-fetch.browser.js is a throwing stub; encrypted-body-fetch binds requests to the verified origin. ehbp 0.3.3 client.js rejects 2xx responses without Ehbp-Response-Nonce and only passes through non-2xx, which SyncEnclaveClient treats as errors. Attestation/verifier correctness is another hunter's area.

webapp-keys-storage.hypothesis: Clerk no-rhc patch (scripts/patch-clerk-worker.mjs) can fail open or load remote code
webapp-keys-storage.why_rejected: Patch only moves the timer worker from a blob: URL to /workers/clerk-timers.js to satisfy worker-src 'self'; both regexes throw if not matched (build fails closed); the no-rhc bundle has no createElement('script')/loadScript, captcha is hard-rejected ('Captcha not supported in this environment'), CSP script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval' is pinned by tests/csp-policy.test.ts. check-clerk-environment.mjs is a CI drift monitor; drift (captcha on) breaks sign-up rather than leaking.

webapp-keys-storage.hypothesis: Passkey rpId 'tinfoil.sh' lets model-authored HTML in the sandbox (webapp-sandbox.tinfoil.sh) obtain the PRF/KEK
webapp-keys-storage.why_rejected: Sandbox vercel.json sends Permissions-Policy publickey-credentials-get=()/create=() and CSP 'sandbox allow-scripts' (opaque origin) on every page. Other tinfoil.sh subdomains could in principle request an assertion with the same salt, but the attacker would still need the wrapped bundle (JWT or DB) and the chain is unverifiable without touching production; the apex rpId is shared with the iOS client by design.

webapp-keys-storage.hypothesis: Unauthenticated authorizationMode in the generic key envelope (plaintext JSON wrapper) lets the controlplane flip 'validated' to 'explicit_start_fresh' and trigger a client-driven start_fresh wipe
webapp-keys-storage.why_rejected: True that the field is unauthenticated, but the only attacker able to edit stored bundles is the controlplane/DB operator, who can delete the rows directly; no confidentiality impact.

webapp-keys-storage.hypothesis: Rollback or substitution of bundles/key_id by the controlplane yields the CEK
webapp-keys-storage.why_rejected: Bundles are AES-GCM under the per-credential KEK; the client verifies derived key_id against the enclave-reported one; substituted/rolled-back bundles only cause recovery failures or use of an older CEK, never key disclosure.

webapp-keys-storage.hypothesis: Cached PRF or CEK cleared incorrectly / sign-out cleanup gaps for non-explicit sign-out (session expiry, remote revocation)
webapp-keys-storage.why_rejected: By design the handler only wipes on explicit sign-out intent (AUTH_SIGNOUT_REQUESTED_AT); session expiry keeps the same user's data. Requires physical/local access; folded into the two low candidates.

webapp-keys-storage.hypothesis: Anonymous (signed-out) chats get uploaded into the next account that signs in on the same browser
webapp-keys-storage.why_rejected: chat-storage.ts:163 marks chats local-only whenever cloud sync is disabled (always when signed out) and sync-predicates.ts:76 never uploads isLocalOnly chats.

webapp-keys-storage.hypothesis: URL fragments (#send=, #settings/, share #key) leak secrets to servers
webapp-keys-storage.why_rejected: #settings/<tab> is a tab name; share key fragment is never sent (Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin, analytics strips fragments and excludes /share). #send= / ?q= auto-submit attacker-chosen prompt text from a link without confirmation (cross-site 'send as the user'), which is not a key issue; left for the rendering/exfil hunters.

webapp-keys-storage.hypothesis: Code-execution derived keys (HKDF of CEK) leave the sealed channel
webapp-keys-storage.why_rejected: code_execution_options.encryptionKey/containerAuthToken are placed in the chat-completion body sealed by EHBP to the router (inference-client.ts:649-652); the feature is gated off by canUseCodeExecution.

webapp-keys-storage.hypothesis: Key history / migration sends CEKs to the wrong place
webapp-keys-storage.why_rejected: migrationKeys() sends primary+alternatives only to /v1/blobs/migrate-all and /v1/search/reindex via the attested sync enclave; history is cleared after fullyMigrated.

webapp-keys-storage.hypothesis: Clerk cookies readable by other tinfoil.sh subdomains (to fetch the user's bundle)
webapp-keys-storage.why_rejected: clerk-js sets __session host-only; only __client_uat (timestamp) is on the eTLD+1; __client is HttpOnly on clerk.tinfoil.sh. FAPI CORS behaviour cannot be verified locally.

ehbp-cross-language.hypothesis: Forged 422 key-config mismatch forces a client to re-key to an unattested HPKE key
ehbp-cross-language.why_rejected: All five SDKs re-attest before rebuilding the transport: tinfoil-go enclave/transport.go clientTransport.RoundTrip -> Handle.invalidate -> refresh -> fetchVerification (nonce-bound document, sigstore + quote + endorsed-machine policy); tinfoil-python _build_ehbp_sync_transport -> self.verify(); tinfoil-js SecureClient.fetch reset()+ready() -> verifyBundle; tinfoil-rs EhbpProxy.refresh_after_mismatch -> set_refresher(verify_rotated_state) and it even rejects a refreshed key equal to the rejected one; tinfoil-swift EHBPVerifiedState.refresh -> handle.verify(). A forged 422 only costs a re-verification plus one replay (re-encrypted).

ehbp-cross-language.hypothesis: Response nonce binding / chunk reordering / replay / cross-request swapping
ehbp-cross-language.why_rejected: Keys are HKDF(exported HPKE secret, salt=enc||server nonce); per-chunk nonce = base XOR seq in all five implementations; reorder/replay/swap fail AEAD (fixtures decrypt-response-reordered-frames, -replayed-frame, -wrong-request-enc, -wrong-nonce pass). Server derives distinct keys per replayed enc because the 32-byte response nonce is fresh; HPKE recipient is created per request so request-side seq restarts without nonce reuse.

ehbp-cross-language.hypothesis: Status code / headers / method / path outside the AEAD (empty AAD) give an exploitable forgery beyond known finding 4
ehbp-cross-language.why_rejected: Confirmed unauthenticated in every implementation, but documented in conformance/SECURITY-AUDIT.md ('method, path, status, and headers are outside AEAD'). Flipping an encrypted 200 to 4xx/5xx only causes errors/retries; 303 with a nonce reduces to finding 4(b); re-targeting an encrypted body to another path/host on the enclave yields a response still sealed to the client. No plaintext or forged-body gain found.

ehbp-cross-language.hypothesis: Nonce-less 2xx plaintext fallback (body substitution) in any client, including old pinned versions
ehbp-cross-language.why_rejected: Go HEAD/v0.3.2/v0.2.x/v0.1.7, JS, Python, Rust and Swift all require Ehbp-Response-Nonce on 2xx for encrypted requests (e2e-missing-nonce-200 / e2e-plaintext-200-failclosed semantics); v0.1.7 even fails closed on all statuses. Duplicate-nonce handling: Go/Python/Rust reject explicitly; JS/Swift reject the coalesced value as invalid hex length.

ehbp-cross-language.hypothesis: 3xx / 303 POST->GET downgrade in the non-Go SDKs (variant of finding 4)
ehbp-cross-language.why_rejected: tinfoil-python builds httpx clients with follow_redirects=False and openai-python raises on any non-2xx; tinfoil-rs and ehbp-rs use reqwest redirect Policy::none(); Node undici follows but the EHBP JS transport checks the final response (no nonce on 2xx -> MissingResponseNonceError), and a consumed-stream re-POST throws TypeError (probed on Node 24); Swift URLSession follows but responseNonceHex(requestWasEncrypted: true) fails closed on the final 2xx. Consistent with finding 4's 'other SDKs not affected'.

ehbp-cross-language.hypothesis: Server middleware: unauthenticated plaintext fallback, error-path leaks, header smuggling, Content-Length retention after decryption
ehbp-cross-language.why_rejected: Production shim cvmimage/tinfoil/cmd/shim/api.go pins EHBP v0.3.2 and composes Middleware -> authorize -> httputil.ReverseProxy; plaintext requests are passed through by design (SPEC 5.2) but gain the gateway nothing it cannot already do with the plaintext Authorization header; error bodies are constant strings; Go's client/transport never writes Header['Content-Length'] or Transfer-Encoding from the map (reqWriteExcludeHeader; h2 encodeHeaders drops them), so the retained header is harmless; response Content-Length is deleted at WriteHeader and the proxy strips upstream Ehbp-Response-Nonce. Request-side frame-boundary truncation yields a clean EOF to the handler (same class as candidate 2; documented in SECURITY-AUDIT.md). v0.3.2 lacks the request-side 64 MiB cap and uses recursion on empty frames (DoS only, documented).

ehbp-cross-language.hypothesis: HPKE enclave key reused by another protocol as a decryption oracle; key persisted where the host can read it
ehbp-cross-language.why_rejected: cvmimage cmd/boot/identity.go generates/loads the key only for EHBP, binds it into the attestation body and the TLS SAN encoding; stored under /mnt/ramdisk/private (0600, ramdisk). No other repo uses the EHBP identity key or the 'ehbp request' info label.

ehbp-cross-language.hypothesis: tinfoil-go NewGateway: catalog and 412 X-Tinfoil-Seal reroute are gateway-controlled, so the gateway chooses which tinfoilsh/* repo and host the prompt is sealed to (model->repo not attested); tinfoil-proxy and confidential-openai-adapter use no ModelPins by default
ehbp-cross-language.why_rejected: Real design weakness but documented in gateway.go ('Catalog maps model names to untrusted repository and replica entries', 'Request model names, not attested identities') with ModelPins/PinnedModelsOnly as the mitigation; exploiting it to read prompts requires Tinfoil (the signer of tinfoilsh/* releases, which the client trusts anyway) to ship a plaintext-leaking image, i.e. it reduces to 'trust Tinfoil's code signing' rather than a new bypass; freshness witnesses bound downgrades to ~7 days. Recorded here so the next round does not redo it; worth a hardening note at most.

ehbp-cross-language.hypothesis: Plaintext cache-prefix header leaks prompt content
ehbp-cross-language.why_rejected: Only tinfoil-go gateway mode sends X-Tinfoil-Cache-Prefix and it is HMAC-SHA256 under a key HKDF-derived from the user cache secret (which only travels inside the sealed body) and the API key; no other SDK emits such a header. Equality linkage of same-prefix requests is inherent to cache routing.

ehbp-cross-language.hypothesis: Session recovery tokens as an attack surface
ehbp-cross-language.why_rejected: All SDKs publish the token in-process only (Go Transport.lastSessionRecoveryToken, JS _lastSessionRecoveryToken, Python _last_token, Rust SessionState, Swift _lastSessionRecoveryToken), clear it on completion/error, and validate 32-byte fields on deserialisation (token-* fixtures). Persistence by the webapp is outside this area and would need a compromised page.

ehbp-cross-language.hypothesis: HTTP/2 GOAWAY/REFUSED_STREAM replay in non-Go clients (finding 1 variants)
