votes.reasoning: Independent code trace on fresh clones at the pinned tags (not the hunter's copies) confirms every file:line claim. (1) EHBP Swift v0.3.2 (8528a8d, pinned `exact: "0.3.2"` by tinfoil-swift HEAD Package.swift and by tinfoil-ios Package.resolved): swift/Sources/EHBP/Client.swift:248-260 `responseNonceHex` returns nil for a nonce-less response whose status is outside 200..<300 even when the request was encrypted; `request()` :100-105 then returns the body untouched and `requestStream()` :175-193 returns a pass-through byte stream. HEAD v0.4.0 (7ee9288) keeps identical logic (:453-465, :106-111, :206-224) and its own UnencryptedResponseTests.swift:31 asserts that 300 passes through, so no fixed release exists. (2) tinfoil-swift v0.8.2 (4988b05) Sources/TinfoilAI/EHBPURLSession.swift performStreamingRequest :382-476 and performRequest :606-638 only inspect 422 application/problem+json for key-config mismatch and otherwise forward the pass-through response (finish(data:...) :469, return (data, response) :635); HEAD 81e07a1 differs only by `verifiedState.current()`. The EHBP URLSession is `.shared` with no URLAuthenticationChallenge handling anywhere in tinfoil-swift or EHBP Swift, so there is no TLS pinning that would stop a WebPKI-capable peer. (3) openai-swift-fork v0.0.15 (c8f8383, also origin/main HEAD; no newer tag): StreamingSession.swift:159-161 only marks statusCode >= 400 as an error, so a 3xx body goes to the SSE interpreter; the non-streaming path (AsyncClient.swift:41-42 -> URLResponseHandler.interceptAndDecode :22-25, and MakeDataTask.swift:19-35 / DataTaskFactory.swift:22-36) never looks at the status at all. (4) tinfoil-ios HEAD cd5824e pins exactly these versions; ChatViewModel.swift:1746 creates TinfoilAI.create(...) with no baseURL (direct to the attested enclave), :4368-4376 sets recoveryStorage=nil for signed-out, temporary, or cloud-sync-disabled chats, :4669-4672 then uses client.chatsStream directly, and :2603/:5884 use client.chats unconditionally; streamed delta.toolCalls become GenUI tool calls (StreamingResponseProcessor.swift:256-275; widgets render_image, render_link_preview, render_message_compose, ...). The recovery path (ChatRecoveryClient.swift:168-196, via api.tinfoil.sh) checks 2xx itself and is unaffected, as the hunter said. PoC reproduced independently: my own Python loopback raw-HTTP peer holding no HPKE key, my own XCTest against tinfoil-swift 0.8.2's TinfoilAI internal initializer (the one create() ends in) built on EHBP 0.3.2 + openai-swift-fork 0.0.15 with only Linux build shims (documented diff). Results: streaming 300 without nonce -> client returned the forged text with finish=stop; non-streaming 500 and 300 without nonce -> forged chat.completion returned; the sealed POST carried Ehbp-Encapsulated-Key and the peer saw neither the prompt nor user_cache_secret. Controls: 200 without nonce rejected on both paths (missingHeader), 404 streaming rejected (statusError), 303->GET->200 rejected. Extra observations: 303->GET->nonce-less 300 is also accepted (redirect-chained variant, no new capability); 304 is delivered bodyless on Linux. I found no missed check: no middleware, no status validation in TinfoilAI, no TLS pinning, no newer fixed release of any of the three packages. Severity: integrity-only forgery of the model's answer by the TLS peer, same class and rating as known Finding 4 but a different SDK, a different downstream library, a separate fix, and a strictly broader non-streaming case (openai-go rejects >=400; openai-swift-fork accepts any status). Finding 4's write-up is silent on Swift, so this is a sibling rather than a duplicate.

votes.attacker_position_assessed: The client's TLS peer; a passive or non-terminating network attacker cannot exploit it. (a) tinfoil-swift users that set `baseURL` to an EHBP forwarding proxy (e.g. the shipped encrypted-request-proxy-example Swift client): the proxy operator, on-path by design, needs no key material and never decrypts the request. (b) Default direct-to-enclave mode, which is what the Tinfoil iOS app uses (TinfoilAI.create with no baseURL): the forger must terminate TLS for the attested router/enclave hostname with a WebPKI-trusted certificate (DNS owner, ACME validation on the enclave IP, CA mis-issuance, or an enterprise TLS-inspection root trusted by the device); the EHBP URLSession is `.shared` with no pinning. The iOS recovery path through api.tinfoil.sh is not exploitable because the app itself requires a 2xx and EHBP rejects 2xx without a nonce.

votes.caveats: RELATED-TO Finding 4 (same vulnerability class: EHBP nonce-less non-2xx pass-through accepted as content by the OpenAI SDK layer), but it is a sibling, not a trivial variant: different SDK and downstream library, separate fix location, strictly broader non-streaming acceptance (any status incl. 500), and it reaches the shipped iOS app; Finding 4's write-up explicitly covers only Go and says nothing about Swift. Reviewers may fold it in as Finding 4b. Linux-only limits of the reproduction: swift-corelibs-foundation suppresses 301/302/303/305-308 as final responses (HTTPURLProtocol.swift ~535), so only the 300 (and bodyless 304) 3xx cases were executed; on Apple platforms 300 is not auto-followed and is delivered as a normal response per standard URLSession semantics, but no Darwin run was possible here, and Location-less 302 behaviour on Apple is unverified. The streaming path needed a Linux shim for URLSession.bytes(for:) and the Go verifier xcframework was removed from the TinfoilAI target (create() replaced by its own internal initializer with a fresh X25519 key); all patches are recorded in evidence/linux-build-patches.diff and do not touch response handling. Impact is integrity only (prompt and user_cache_secret stay sealed). Whether any certificate-capable on-path party can realistically reach the router hostname in production was not assessed (no production traffic sent). Non-streaming 4xx acceptance was derived from code, not executed (500 and 300 were).
